name: ambiguous
why: MOVED FROM callers/callees TO dossier (gh#372). Those two tools are gone — their rows
are dossier's `callers`/`callees` fields — and the block had to move with them, or the
warning would have been deleted along with the surface that carried it.
It is MORE necessary here, not less. This repo's own recorded finding is that
`candidates` disambiguates the IDENTITY of the described symbol while nothing
disambiguates the EDGES attributed to it: dossier('_classify') names three same-named
functions in `candidates` and then lists the union of all three functions' neighbours
at confidence 'exact', because corroboration means three layers agreed and all three
resolve by name. A reader who checks `candidates` and then reads `callers` is still
misled. So the tool a model is told to call FIRST is exactly where the block belongs.
The withholding clause is GONE and that is a real difference: the deleted tools capped
an ambiguous list at a sample of 8 and said `count` was still the true total. The
composite dossier never capped, and adding a cap in order to warn about it would
change what a call returns. So the block now discloses only — trimming is the byte
budget's job and it discloses separately, in `_limited`.
Measured on the public entropic index: `size` matches 9 distinct signatures and
returns 331 caller rows, 330 of them shared with its eight namesakes. Every one of
those rows already said confidence='fuzzy', and that was not enough, because fuzzy is
a three-value enum over a quantity that is a NUMBER.
text: An `ambiguous` block means the name matched several signatures: the neighbour rows are SHARED with all of them, so do not attribute them to one until you re-ask with `qualified`.
